evidence.title: File:Duck and Preserved Mustard Green Soup - Little Beijing complimentary with duck (4713827305).jpg
evidence.description:
It's funny how a Beijing Duck restaurant is named 喜鹊楼, or Magpie House. Collingwood supporters perhaps? :)
  The 北京鸭 Beijing Duck is good, roasted, and then flash fried to crisp up the skin before serving. For AUD45.80, you can get the rest of the duck meat stir-fried with beansprouts, or for an extra AUD5 stirfried with noodles. We opt for the beansprouts and they come out smoky from a hot wok, glistening with duck fat and the beansprouts still crunchy. The 2-dish set is good value.
  The other dishes are rather simple though, with the 椒盐豆腐 Salt and Pepper Tofu silky inside, but with a thick, soggy crust. The 糖醋排骨 sweet vinegar ribs were nice, not again, nothing special.
  喜鹊楼 Little Beijing House Chinese Restaurant
(03) 9878 9784
144A Canterbury Rd,
Blackburn South VIC 3130

evidence.title: File:Liat Portal for Foodie Disorder – Fried Egg on Whole Grain Bread with Fresh Vegetables.jpg
evidence.description: High quality photograph by Liat Portal showing a simple home prepared meal made in Tel Aviv, featuring a fried egg with basil leaves placed on whole grain bread with cottage cheese, accompanied by fresh chopped tomatoes, cucumber, and red bell pepper. This image documents basic cooking skills accessible to anyone, nutrition built from limited ingredients, and cooking without formal training, emphasizing food education by time and by budget rather than technique. It reflects early nutritional literacy, confidence building through repetition, and food as a daily safety and stability mechanism, demonstrating how regional, everyday meals can support long term health awareness, self sufficiency, and future food system resilience, as part of the Foodie Disorder global food culture archive.
